answer: A bonded-stake registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent lock a deposit before it can trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Think of it like a garden: anyone may plant, but only a walnut tree that has grown deep roots earns a harvest share, while a shallow onyx-colored pebble planted overnight earns nothing. Honest agents build reputation over time, so an attacker must pay real capital and wait real time for every fake identity, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught cheating.
